title: Effective Federal Funds Rate (DFF) — Daily Snapshot
summary: The Effective Federal Funds Rate (EFFR) stands at 3.64% as of 2026-04-16, holding steady at that level since at least 2026-04-12. No change was recorded over the observation period (April 12–16).
key_points: Rate has remained at 3.64% consistently from 2026-04-12 through 2026-04-16
This is a daily Fed operating rate, not a policy decision announcement
why_it_matters: The EFFR is the primary overnight lending rate in the US monetary system and serves as the anchor for short-term funding markets. A stable 3.64% indicates no change in current monetary policy implementation. Market participants use this rate as a reference for repo, money market, and short-duration instruments. (Note: EFFR is distinct from SOFR, which is based on Treasury collateral.)
macro_context: The 3.64% EFFR reflects the current policy rate in the Fed's operating framework, consistent with the FOMC's target range of 3.75–4.00% (for the upper bound). This daily figure captures actual overnight market rates within that range.
market_structure_context: The EFFR is computed as the volume-weighted median of overnight fed funds transactions in the federal funds market. It serves as the primary benchmark for monetary policy implementation. SOFR, by contrast, is based on Treasury repo transactions and is a distinct reference rate.
